lessonRef.subject: financial-literacy
lessonRef.title: Mastery check: a one-week simulated budget

objective: Learners build a one-week simulated budget with fixed and flexible categories for a fictional character, apply a surprise simulated expense partway through the week, and revise the plan so it still balances against a fixed weekly amount.
scenario: This is a fictional, simulated scenario with no real money involved: a made-up fourth grader named Malik has $12.00 of simulated spending money for one week, already planning $3.00 for simulated savings as a fixed category every week.
materials: the fictional budget table on this task sheet

tasks.directions: Malik's original simulated plan for the week: savings (fixed) $3.00, a simulated snack (flexible) $5.00, a simulated bus fare (fixed) $1.50.

prompts.text: What is the total of Malik's original three planned amounts?
Out of Malik's $12.00, how much is left unplanned after these three amounts?

tasks.directions: Midweek, a simulated surprise expense of $4.00 for a replacement school-supply item comes up, and Malik must fit it into the same $12.00 total without touching the fixed $3.00 savings.

prompts.text: Adding the $4.00 surprise expense to the original three amounts, what is the new total?
Does the new total fit inside Malik's $12.00 without reducing any category?

tasks.directions: Since the new total does not fit, Malik must reduce one flexible category (not the fixed savings or the fixed bus fare) so the week balances exactly at $12.00.

prompts.text: By exactly how much must the flexible snack category be reduced for the week to balance at $12.00?

tasks.directions: Think about the difference between fixed and flexible categories.

prompts.text: Explain why Malik reduced the flexible snack category instead of the fixed savings or fixed bus fare when the surprise expense came up.

remediation: If a learner reduces a fixed category instead of a flexible one, reteach with two labeled envelopes, fixed and flexible, sorting each planned amount into the correct envelope before deciding which envelope a surprise expense can pull from.
extension: Have the learner build their own one-week simulated budget with one fixed and two flexible categories, then apply a surprise expense of their own choosing and show the rebalanced total.
